sentences.text: Erliansaurus was a small to medium-sized therizinosaur, a group of dinosaurs estimated to reach lengths between 2.6 and 4 meters and weigh between 91 and 400 kilograms.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a partial skeleton of a subadult that includes vertebrae, a scapula, pelvic fragments, leg bones, and partial foot bones, but lacks any skull traces.
This animal was a bipedal herbivore, walking on two legs while feeding on plants.

The specific name bellamanus means "beautiful hand" in Latin, referencing the exquisite preservation of the forelimb which features enormous, strongly recurved and pointed claws, with the thumb claw being the largest.
Fossils of Erliansaurus were discovered near Sanhangobi in Inner Mongolia in 1999.
The type species Erliansaurus bellamanus was described by Xu Xing and colleagues in 2002, with the holotype specimen LH V0002 coming from the Santonian stage of the Iren Dabasu Formation.
The original describers assigned Erliansaurus to Therizinosauroidea in a basal position, suggesting it was likely not a therizinosaurid.
However, some early cladistic analyses recovered Erliansaurus as a basal member of the Therizinosauridae, a classification now supported by the Paleobi Database.
Fossil evidence places Erliansaurus in the Campanian stage, ranging from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
